MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #10
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which of these shows 841 in words? (1 mark)
   A. eight hundred and forty-one
   B. eight hundred and fourteen
   C. eight hundred and fifty-one
   D. nine hundred and forty-one

2. Round 47 to the nearest ten. (1 mark)
   A. 40
   B. 50
   C. 0
   D. 60

3. What is the smallest 5-digit number? (1 mark)
   A. 99,999
   B. 1,000
   C. 9,999
   D. 10,000

4. Which Roman numeral stands for 7? (1 mark)
   A. VIIII
   B. VX
   C. VII
   D. IIII

5. Work out 1,856 + 4,567. (1 mark)
   A. 6,323
   B. 6,423
   C. 5,313
   D. 6,433

6. Which number must be added to 3,425 to make 5,743? (1 mark)
   A. 2,318
   B. 9,168
   C. 2,418
   D. 2,308

7. Why can we add 3,875 + 2,450 in either order? (1 mark)
   A. The sum changes when the order changes
   B. The answer is always the bigger number
   C. Only the bigger number can go first
   D. The sum stays the same when numbers are added in any order

8. One county has 7,300 pupils and a smaller county has 4,562 pupils. How many more pupils does the bigger county have? (1 mark)
   A. 2,728 pupils
   B. 2,738 pupils
   C. 2,838 pupils
   D. 3,262 pupils

9. What is 24 × 30? (1 mark)
   A. 7,200
   B. 72
   C. 54
   D. 720

10. What is 72 ÷ 6? (1 mark)
   A. 12
   B. 13
   C. 11
   D. 22

11. 38 mangoes are shared equally among 5 children. How many mangoes are left over? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 4
   C. 2
   D. 3

12. A rectangle is cut into 5 equal parts and 2 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 5/2
   B. 2/5
   C. 2/3
   D. 3/5

13. Which fraction of an hour is 15 minutes? (1 mark)
   A. 1/2
   B. 1/3
   C. 3/4
   D. 1/4

14. What is 3/4 of 12? (1 mark)
   A. 7
   B. 9
   C. 12
   D. 3

15. A rectangle is cut into 8 equal parts and 3 of the parts are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded? (1 mark)
   A. 8/3
   B. 3/8
   C. 5/8
   D. 3/5

16. A hundred square has 5 of its small squares shaded. Which decimal shows the shaded part? (1 mark)
   A. 0.05
   B. 0.005
   C. 0.5
   D. 5

17. If x = 4, what is the value of 10 − x? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 40
   C. 14
   D. 104

18. Which expression shows "a number y shared equally among 4 people"? (1 mark)
   A. y + 4
   B. y − 4
   C. 4y
   D. y ÷ 4

19. Simplify 3m + 2o + m + 4o. (1 mark)
   A. 3m + 6o
   B. 6m + 4o
   C. 4m + 6o
   D. 10mo

20. Change 7 m 60 cm to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 67 cm
   B. 760 cm
   C. 130 cm
   D. 7,600 cm

21. A rectangle is made of 7 rows with 9 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 70 square units
   B. 63 square units
   C. 32 square units
   D. 16 square units

22. How many 1/4 L cups can be filled from 3 L of milk? (1 mark)
   A. 6
   B. 12
   C. 9
   D. 7

23. Change 48 hours to days. (1 mark)
   A. 4 days
   B. 0.8 days
   C. 3 days
   D. 2 days

24. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 11 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 1. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 11:55
   B. 11:01
   C. 12:05
   D. 11:05

25. Change 150 minutes to hours and minutes. (1 mark)
   A. 3 h 30 min
   B. 2 h
   C. 2 h 30 min
   D. 3 h

26. Wekesa wakes up at half past six in the morning. How do we write this time? (1 mark)
   A. 6:30 a.m.
   B. 6:30 noon
   C. 6:03 a.m.
   D. 6:30 p.m.

27. Two quarter turns together make (1 mark)
   A. a full turn
   B. a half turn
   C. a three-quarter turn
   D. a quarter turn

28. Which shape has three straight sides? (1 mark)
   A. Rectangle
   B. Triangle
   C. Circle
   D. Square

29. A group of five tally marks is drawn by (1 mark)
   A. four upright strokes crossed by a fifth stroke
   B. five separate circles
   C. two long lines
   D. a square

30. Which is the safest way to count vehicles for a data project? (1 mark)
   A. Standing in the middle of the road
   B. Sitting on the road
   C. From a safe place inside the school gate with a teacher
   D. Running alongside the vehicles

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Work out 4 L − 1 3/4 L. Show your working. (3 marks)

32. A triangle has sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm. Find its perimeter. (2 marks)

33. Write 0.7, 0.07, 0.75 and 0.57 in order from the smallest to the largest. (3 marks)

34. List all the factors of 36. (3 marks)

35. The minute hand of a clock points to 4 and the hour hand is just past 9. What time is it? Explain how you know. (3 marks)

36. Wanjiru buys 4 loaves of bread at Ksh 60 each, 2 packets of sugar at Ksh 155 each and 1 tin of cooking fat at Ksh 480. She pays with Ksh 2,000. (a) Find the total cost. (b) Find her change. (5 marks)

37. Divide 84 by 4 and check your answer. (3 marks)

38. Wanjiku has 2 L of milk and buys 1 1/2 L more. How much milk does she have now? (2 marks)

39. Draw an angle using a ruler. Name the vertex and the arms and mark the angle with a small curve. (3 marks)

40. Write 5x + 3y − 2x + y in its simplest form. (3 marks)

41. Explain how you can use addition to check a subtraction. Use 7,865 − 3,542 = 4,323 as an example. (3 marks)

42. A tank holds 20 L of water. In the morning 4 1/2 L is taken out and in the afternoon 3 3/4 L is taken out. How much water is left in the tank? (5 marks)

43. On a poultry farm each of 16 hens lays 21 eggs in one month. How many eggs are laid altogether? (3 marks)

44. Explain why 0.5 is greater than 0.45 even though 0.45 has more digits. (3 marks)

45. Write the steps for collecting and recording data about the favourite colours of 10 friends. (4 marks)

46. Kamau buys 15 packets of sweets and each packet has 40 sweets. How many sweets does he have? (2 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — MOCK EXAM #10 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — eight hundred and forty-one
   841 = eight hundred and forty-one. Say the hundreds, then "and", then the tens and ones.

2. B — 50
   Look at the ones digit 7. It is 5 or more, so go up to the next ten. 47 rounds to 50.

3. D — 10,000
   Adding 1 to 9,999 gives 10,000, the smallest number with five digits.

4. C — VII
   7 is written VII. Letters after a bigger letter are added.

5. B — 6,423
   Add ones, tens, hundreds and thousands, regrouping when a column is 10 or more. 1,856 + 4,567 = 6,423.

6. A — 2,318
   5,743 − 3,425 = 2,318. Check: 3,425 + 2,318 = 5,743.

7. D — The sum stays the same when numbers are added in any order
   Addition can be done in any order: 3,875 + 2,450 = 2,450 + 3,875 = 6,325.

8. B — 2,738 pupils
   Subtract 7,300 − 4,562 = 2,738. Check by adding: 2,738 + 4,562 = 7,300.

9. D — 720
   24 × 3 = 72, then × 10 gives 720.

10. A — 12
   6 × 12 = 72, so 72 ÷ 6 = 12.

11. D — 3
   38 ÷ 5 = 7 remainder 3. Each child gets 7 and 3 are left.

12. B — 2/5
   The whole has 5 equal parts and 2 are shaded, so 2/5 is shaded.

13. D — 1/4
   15 × 4 = 60, so 15 minutes is one quarter of an hour.

14. B — 9
   12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 3 × 3 = 9. So 3/4 of 12 is 9.

15. B — 3/8
   The whole has 8 equal parts and 3 are shaded, so 3/8 is shaded.

16. A — 0.05
   5 out of 100 squares is 5/100 = 0.05.

17. A — 6
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 6.

18. D — y ÷ 4
   The key words tell us the operation. "a number y shared equally among 4 people" is written y ÷ 4.

19. C — 4m + 6o
   Only like terms can be joined. 3m + 2o + m + 4o = 4m + 6o.

20. B — 760 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 7 × 100 = 700, and 700 + 60 = 760. So the answer is 760 cm.

21. B — 63 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 7 × 9 = 63 square units.

22. B — 12
   Each litre fills 4 cups, so 3 L fills 3 × 4 = 12 cups.

23. D — 2 days
   48 ÷ 24 = 2 days.

24. D — 11:05
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 1 shows 1 × 5 = 5 minutes, so the time is 11:05.

25. C — 2 h 30 min
   150 ÷ 60 = 2 remainder 30, so 150 minutes = 2 h 30 min.

26. A — 6:30 a.m.
   Times from midnight to noon use a.m. and times from noon to midnight use p.m. The correct answer is 6:30 a.m..

27. B — a half turn
   1/4 + 1/4 = 1/2, so two quarter turns make a half turn.

28. B — Triangle
   A triangle has three straight sides and three corners.

29. A — four upright strokes crossed by a fifth stroke
   The fifth stroke crosses the first four to make a group of five.

30. C — From a safe place inside the school gate with a teacher
   Safety comes first. Count from a safe place and never stand in the road.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 1/4 L
   Working / marking points: Change 4 L to 3 4/4 L (1 mark). 3 4/4 − 1 3/4 = 2 1/4 (1 mark). Check: 2 1/4 + 1 3/4 = 4 L (1 mark).

32. (2 marks)
   Answer: 12 cm
   Working / marking points: 3 + 4 + 5 = 12. 1 mark for adding all three sides and 1 mark for the unit.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.07, 0.57, 0.7, 0.75
   Working / marking points: Write with two decimal places: 0.70, 0.07, 0.75, 0.57. 1 mark for 0.07 first, 2 marks for the rest in order.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36
   Working / marking points: Pairs: 1 × 36, 2 × 18, 3 × 12, 4 × 9, 6 × 6. 3 marks for all nine factors, 2 marks for seven or eight, 1 mark for at least five.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: 9:20. Each number is worth 5 minutes, so the minute hand at 4 shows 4 × 5 = 20 minutes past 9.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 9:20, 1 mark for 5 minutes per number, 1 mark for 4 × 5.

36. (5 marks)
   Answer: (a) Ksh 1,030 (b) Ksh 970
   Working / marking points: 4 × 60 = 240 (1 mark); 2 × 155 = 310 (1 mark); 240 + 310 + 480 = 1,030 (1 mark); 2,000 − 1,030 = 970 (2 marks).

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: 21
   Working / marking points: 80 ÷ 4 = 20 (1 mark); 4 ÷ 4 = 1, so 21 (1 mark); check 21 × 4 = 84 (1 mark).

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 L
   Working / marking points: 2 + 1 1/2 = 3 1/2. 1 mark for the addition and 1 mark for the unit.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: A drawing with two straight lines meeting at a point, the point labelled vertex, the lines labelled arms and a curve between them.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for two straight arms, 1 mark for the vertex, 1 mark for the curve.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3x + 4y
   Working / marking points: x terms: 5x − 2x = 3x (1 mark). y terms: 3y + y = 4y (1 mark). Answer 3x + 4y (1 mark).

41. (3 marks)
   Answer: Add the answer to the number that was taken away: 4,323 + 3,542 = 7,865, which is the starting number, so the subtraction is correct.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for saying add the answer and the smaller number, 1 mark for the example, 1 mark for saying the result matches the starting number.

42. (5 marks)
   Answer: 11 3/4 L
   Working / marking points: Total taken: 4 1/2 + 3 3/4 = 4 2/4 + 3 3/4 = 7 5/4 = 8 1/4 L (3 marks). 20 − 8 1/4 = 11 3/4 L (2 marks).

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: 336 eggs
   Working / marking points: 21 × 6 = 126 (1 mark); 21 × 10 = 210 (1 mark); 126 + 210 = 336 (1 mark).

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: 0.5 = 0.50. Comparing tenths, 5 tenths is more than 4 tenths, so 0.50 is greater than 0.45. The number of digits does not decide the size.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for writing 0.5 as 0.50, 1 mark for comparing tenths, 1 mark for the conclusion.

45. (4 marks)
   Answer: Decide the question; ask each friend and make a tally mark; draw a table with a title and headings; write the totals and check they add up to 10.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: 600 sweets
   Working / marking points: 15 × 4 = 60 (1 mark), then × 10 = 600 (1 mark).
